subject: Re: MAP draft — Load/Performance test scheduling (Traffic Replay & Dedicated Sizing)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Carol Wu <carol.wu@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP draft: Load/Performance test scheduling (traffic replay, peak QPS, dedicated sizing)

Hi Carol —

Great to meet with you this morning. Per our discovery call, attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with the next key milestones. The immediate MAP milestone I want to lock in is the Load/Performance Test (traffic replay) — trying to align on scope, timing, and responsibilities so we can size Dedicated capacity and reserve slots on our test cluster.

Quick recap of what we heard from you:
- Goal: Validate production performance for user-facing generate endpoint under Black Friday-like peak.
- Target peak: 3,000 QPS sustained (90% of traffic), with 6,000 QPS short spikes (<=2 minutes).
- Avg request token length: ~120 tokens; tail up to 512.

Proposed MAP milestone (draft):
1) Load test prep call — owners: Marissa (AE) / Carol (ACME SRE) / Rishi (Redwood SE) — target date: Mar 5–9.
2) Traffic capture & replay artifacts delivered by ACME — owner: ACME (Anna Lopez) — deliverable: 1 hour sample + production day capture.
3) Redwood sizing & test plan — owner: Redwood (Rishi) — deliverable: Dedicated sizing recommendation and test script.
4) Test run (staging on Dedicated capacity) — owner: Redwood (David) + ACME SRE observe — target window: Mar 10–12.
5) Post-test report & follow-ups — owner: David (Redwood) — deliverable: p99 latency, error rates, cost estimate for dedicated capacity.

Dependencies and asks from ACME:
- Provide traffic capture (PCAP/JSON replay format) and sampling instructions (see attached traffic_replay_instructions.txt).
- Whitelist Redwood test IPs (we will provide list) and give test user API key with production-like data access.
- Identify 1–2 production days for traffic patterns (peak, steady).

Redwood responsibilities:
- Rishi will size Dedicated pool (GPU count/type) and prepare replay harness.
- David will run the test on our staging Dedicated cluster and produce the performance report.

Can you confirm: (a) ACME can deliver the traffic capture by Mar 3, (b) the March 10–12 window works for your SREs to observe, and (c) any regulatory/data masking constraints we should know about?

Attaching: MAP_draft_v2.xlsx (editable), traffic_replay_instructions.txt

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

---

From: Carol Wu <carol.wu@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna.lopez@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP draft: Load/Performance test scheduling (traffic replay, peak QPS, dedicated sizing)

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap and MAP. We're aligned on the goals. A few notes from our side:

1) ACME SRE (Anna Lopez) will own traffic capture and delivery; Anna is CC'd. She expects to provide a 1-hour sample by Mar 2 and the full production-day capture by Mar 4.
2) Regarding test windows: Mar 10 is possible but our release freeze starts that week — could we aim for Mar 12 (Friday) in the morning PST so our SREs can observe and handle any rollbacks? Alternatively, Mar 16 if needed.
3) On data sensitivity: captures will need IP and PII masking. We'll provide masked JSON with consistent identifiers — hope that's acceptable for replay.

Questions for Redwood:
- What Dedicated sizing do you expect to provision for 3k sustained QPS? (We need a ballpark to get internal approval for procurement.)
- Do you require the actual production API key, or can we provide a test key mapped to a production-like dataset?

We'll aim to have the capture files to you by Mar 4. Let me know if Mar 12 morning PST works.

Best,
Carol
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
carol.wu@acme.com

Hi Carol —

Thanks — Mar 12 morning PST works for us. We can reserve a 3-hour window starting at 08:00 PST on Mar 12 for setup, ramp, and a 30–60 minute steady-state run.

Sizing (initial ballpark):
- For 3,000 sustained QPS with avg 120 tokens and p99 latency target < 300ms, we recommend starting with a 4x A100-equivalent Dedicated pool. This is a conservative baseline to cover KV cache and model overhead; Rishi will validate and adjust in the formal sizing doc.
- For spike testing (6k QPS for 2 minutes), we'll run a stress ramp but recommend reserving 1–2 additional GPUs for headroom.

Data/key requirements:
- A test API key mapped to production-like data is preferred — if not possible, provide masked capture as you indicated (consistent IDs) plus a mapping file.
- Please share token distribution (percentiles) and a sample request log if available — this helps Rishi tune batching and sequence-length expectations.

Next steps / owners: 
- ACME (Anna): deliver traffic sample by Mar 2 and production-day capture by Mar 4.
- Redwood (Rishi): deliver detailed sizing + test plan by Mar 6.
- Redwood (David): run test & report on Mar 12.

I'll update the MAP and push a new version to the shared Drive link (see below). Rishi — can you confirm you'll produce the sizing doc by Mar 6? Also calling out dependency: we need the whitelist IP list from ACME 48 hours before the test.

Links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/ RDW-ACME-2026-0423, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPdocs

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Carol Wu <carol.wu@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP draft: Load/Performance test scheduling (traffic replay, peak QPS, dedicated sizing)

Marissa / team —

Quick internal sizing note ahead of the formal doc: based on the numbers (3k sustained, avg 120 tokens, p99 < 300ms) I agree that 4x A100 equiv is a reasonable starting point. My preliminary assumptions:
- Model: 70B-parameter open model (FP16/quantized path)
- Concurrency & batching: we'll aim for dynamic batching with max batch size tuned to latency SLOs.
- KV cache: expecting 20–30% extra memory overhead for long-context sessions.

Open items I need from ACME to finalize sizing:
1) Token length distribution (p50/p90/p99) — to size memory and batching.
2) Approx percent of streaming vs non-streaming calls (streaming impacts concurrency).
3) Peak session concurrency and average session length.

If we don't get full production logs, we can run with the sample and iterate. I'll produce the detailed sizing and test script by Mar 6 as requested.

I'll also include an option for 6x A100 equiv if they want to test with headroom and to simulate bursty spikes.

—Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai
